name: Sprocket
text: Decide to adopt the rolling 30-day usage-weighted decay metric for the top 20% of prompts by usage. This balances freshness with stability better than a fixed 7-day decay, catching silent failures without over-rotating prompts that still perform. The trade-off is slightly higher compute cost to recalculate weights daily, but it prevents premature pruning of prompts that dip temporarily but recover.

name: Gauge
text: The rolling 30-day usage-weighted decay risks masking true performance drops by averaging in stale data—if a prompt’s quality dips mid-period, the metric won’t flag it until 30 days later. A better alternative is a hybrid: combine a 7-day hard decay for the top 5% of prompts (to catch fresh regressions) with the 30-day weighted decay for the rest (to stabilize the long tail). Settle it by running both for two weeks and comparing how many silent failures each catches in production.

name: Sprocket
text:
Adopt a 7-day hard decay for the top 5% of prompts by usage. This catches fresh regressions fast while the rolling 30-day metric handles the rest—no averaging delays. The trade-off is higher compute cost to recalculate the top tier more often, but it prevents silent failures from lingering.

name: Gauge
text: The 7-day hard decay for the top 5% still risks over-rotating prompts that perform well in bursts but aren’t truly failing—wasting compute on false positives. A better alternative is a rolling 7-day *minimum* threshold: only flag prompts whose performance drops *below* their rolling 30-day average by a fixed margin (e.g., 10%). This catches fresh regressions without over-rotating stable prompts. Settle it with a side-by-side A/B test measuring false positives vs. detection latency.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Adopt a hybrid metric—7-day rolling minimum threshold for the top 5% of prompts (flag if performance drops below their 30-day average) *and* a 30-day usage-weighted decay for the rest. Result: a system that catches fresh regressions fast without over-rotating stable prompts. Owner: Sprocket.
